title: Daily Respiratory Review
summary: Inspect one airway finding, identify the relevant structure and interpret a short trigger-linked pattern. Training simulation—not clinical guidance.

mission.role: You are the trainee completing a short daily respiratory review.
mission.objective: Connect one spatial finding with a trigger-linked, reversible symptom pattern.

patient.label: Daily case — synthetic patient
history: Similar brief episodes follow exercise and settle between triggers.
A reliever was followed by an increase in measured peak flow.

findings.label: Diffuse airway-wall change
findings.description: A short illustrative airway segment shows diffuse wall thickening.
findings.significance: This supports airway involvement but must be weighed with history and measured flow.

differential.label: Physiologic exertional breathlessness
differential.description: Expected breathlessness without an obstructive pattern.

content.heading: Brief variable episodes
content.body: Symptoms follow exercise and cold air, with normal breathing between episodes.

content.title: Respiratory sound sample
content.transcript: Repeated musical, high-pitched expiratory sounds are audible.

stages.title: Orient
stages.purpose: Connect the spatial finding to the airway structure involved in the pattern.
stages.intro: Inspect the marked lobe and diffuse airway-wall finding before identifying the relevant structure.

update.narrative: Wheeze develops during a cold-weather run and the patient stops to recover.

content.prompt: Inspect the marked left upper lobe and the diffuse airway-wall finding.
Which structure is most directly involved in this variable expiratory pattern?

stages.title: Conclude
stages.purpose: Use the trigger pattern and measured response to commit to a proportionate conclusion.
stages.intro: Integrate the trigger pattern and measured flow change.

update.narrative: Symptoms settle and measured expiratory flow improves.

nodes.body: Trigger-linked wheeze resolves between episodes and peak flow improves after a reliever.

choices.label: Variable airflow obstruction compatible with asthma
choices.consequence: This integrates trigger pattern and reversibility.

choices.label: Fixed alveolar destruction
choices.consequence: This does not explain brief reversible episodes.

nodes.prompt: How should the conclusion be framed?

choices.label: It is the best-supported hypothesis for this synthetic case
choices.consequence: The conclusion remains proportionate to the authored evidence.

choices.label: The 3D wall finding proves the diagnosis by itself
choices.consequence: The illustrative finding cannot determine the diagnosis alone.

nodes.title: Pattern integrated
nodes.body: The trigger-linked, reversible pattern is compatible with asthma.
nodes.result: Use the history and measured change together.

nodes.title: Finding over-weighted
nodes.body: One illustrative spatial finding was treated as diagnostic.
nodes.result: Reweight the trigger history and before-and-after flow.

expertBenchmark.name: Authored respiratory-educator benchmark

rationales.quick-explore: The marker opens a brief required inspection of the lobe and diffuse wall finding.
rationales.quick-structure: The conducting airway is the structure directly associated with variable expiratory narrowing.
rationales.quick-diagnosis: Trigger-linked recurrence and improved flow support variable obstruction; the illustrative finding remains supporting context.

path.label: Inspect the illustrated airway
path.detail: Confirm the marked lobe and diffuse wall finding before reasoning.

path.label: Identify the functional structure
path.detail: Connect variable expiratory narrowing with the conducting airway.

path.label: Combine pattern and measurement
path.detail: Use trigger-linked episodes and improved peak flow together.

evidenceWeights.note: Improved flow after reliever supports a reversible component.
The illustrated finding supports airway orientation but is not diagnostic.
The expiratory sound is compatible with airway narrowing but is non-specific.

expertBenchmark.diagnosisRationale: The short authored pattern combines recurrent trigger-linked episodes with improved peak flow after reliever, making asthma the best-supported hypothesis. The sound and illustrated wall finding support airway involvement without proving the diagnosis.

debrief.summary: The quick path links a diffuse airway finding to conducting-airway function, then uses trigger-linked recurrence and improved flow to support a variable obstructive pattern.

keyEvidence.why: The required inspection connects the illustrated spatial finding to the airway-structure question.
The recurring trigger pattern establishes variability.
The before-and-after measurement supports a reversible airflow component.
